hypothesis: Input-validity changes in positive success tests require a new applicability proof. A narrow existing expected-exception template can provide a more stable rejection obligation, but syntax alone does not prove that the changed input belongs to the rejected class.
policy: Apply the same source predicate to all fixed round09 candidates. Preserve all ranks; no refill. Then retain original complete-test semantic support and the complete eligible native prefix. Missing required native outcomes stop without an alert. Never replace after independent audit.
classification_scope: One direct bound pytest.raises region containing one direct imported operation. No additional lexical assert or control flow. Source syntax classification only; complete contract review still has to bind the changed field to the required rejection.
development_limitation: Designed after round09 results were audited. This is a retrospective development ablation. It is not heldout evidence or a new test constructor.
novelty: No separate novelty claim for recognizing an exception template. This tests whether distinguishing success obligations from rejection obligations improves the earlier input-validity construction.

validation.scope: Source bindings, UTF-8 receipt boundary, mixed/indirect templates, complete-candidate coverage, historical-prefix gaps, first-failure stops and exact whole-alert transfer

classification_limitations: Top-level syntax does not establish that the edited field causes rejection.
Nested argument calls, fixture/setup effects, callable assertion helpers and dynamic monkeypatches remain full-test review obligations.
Eligible is a construction-form label, not a validity label.
provenance_repair: Freeze all actually loaded local verifier modules, not only named entrypoints.
